mbm-1451.clue: I keep one pin on my bookshelf.
mbm-1451.quote: When our little bowling alley replaced its old pins, the owner gave me the one with a blue paint mark. It has become a very tall bookend. Every time I dust it I apologize for the scratches.

mbm-1452.clue: I hide the stitching in the rain.
mbm-1452.quote: My latest quilt shows the red roofs of our block in a downpour. The long straight stitches that hold the layers together are the streaks of rain. It took a week to finish the weather.

mbm-1453.clue: I carry the quietest timer in the gym.
mbm-1453.quote: My friend gave me a little sandglass for resting between weight sets. I turn it over on the bench and watch the last grains fall. It never beeps over anyone’s favorite song.

mbm-1454.clue: I left the sunflower on the fairway.
mbm-1454.quote: A sunflower sprang up beside a bench at our course. I took a picture of Dad lining up a putt behind it. In the photo he looks like the tiniest golfer in an enormous garden.

mbm-1455.clue: I take a photograph of the wrong corner.
mbm-1455.quote: A hundred people stood facing the statue. I turned around and photographed a little girl drawing all their backs in blue chalk. Her paper city was the best sight I saw that afternoon.

mbm-1456.clue: I brought the cloud home in pencil.
mbm-1456.quote: After my second parachute jump I sketched the shadow of our canopy crossing a pale field. It looked like a cloud with a tail. My instructor added one dot underneath and said that dot was me.

mbm-1457.clue: My first ski tracks ended at a sandwich.
mbm-1457.quote: I followed Dad’s neat turns down the practice slope to a bench where Mum had lunch waiting. The photograph shows two trails and one trail of crumbs. I can still tell you which way home we took.

mbm-1458.clue: Our club has one slow song for tying shoes.
mbm-1458.quote: The DJ knows the crowd is dancing hard when the first loose lace appears. He put on a slow number and four of us knelt together. We stood back up just in time for the chorus.

mbm-1459.clue: I found my missing thumb beside the jam.
mbm-1459.quote: I kept a painted prop thumb for a magic trick in the kitchen cupboard. Dad moved it beside the preserves. The next morning both of us reached for what we thought was a ripe strawberry.

mbm-1460.clue: I'll never get that grape back in the bowl.
mbm-1460.quote: At family parties I photograph the fruit before anyone starts eating. My best still life has my nephew's little fist sneaking a grape. I enlarged just that bit for his mum.

mbm-1461.clue: I started with three potatoes of equal dignity.
mbm-1461.quote: I practiced juggling over the laundry basket so the potatoes wouldn’t bruise. One came flying back out whenever the others hit the bottom. I told Mum the basket wanted a turn too.

mbm-1462.clue: I write from the wrong end of the street.
mbm-1462.quote: I drew my story’s town looking down from a church tower, then rewrote the scene from the view of a kid under an open umbrella. All the important things suddenly happened at shoe level.

mbm-1463.clue: I counted my dumplings with ribbons.
mbm-1463.quote: At the fair each contestant tied a ribbon to the rail after finishing a plate. My little sister chose the colors for mine. I came fourth and went home with the prettiest section of fence.

mbm-1464.clue: I take a bow to the carpenter first.
mbm-1464.quote: As the curtain operator I spend the whole play beside the wooden frame our set builder made. At curtain call I give the frame a little knock. From the other side he always knocks back.

mbm-1465.clue: I found a shortcut for a snail.
mbm-1465.quote: I played a slow little garden game with Mum and made a bridge from a fallen pixel leaf. The snail arrived at its lettuce before either of us understood the controls. Mum declared us expert gardeners.

mbm-1466.clue: I have a blanket for the commercial breaks.
mbm-1466.quote: I spread it over the coffee table and draw our guesses about the next scene on little slips of paper. When the pajama movie resumes, the guesses go undercover until the ending.

mbm-1467.clue: I know the sound of a heron taking off.
mbm-1467.quote: I was watching tiny reeds shake through my binoculars when a heron lifted straight out of the water beside me. I missed the photo. The great rushing slap of its wings stayed with me all the way home.

mbm-1468.clue: I bought a door knob without a door.
mbm-1468.quote: The glass knob at the junk shop had a blue swirl caught inside. I fixed it to the lid of my tool chest. Every repair now begins with opening a very small, very fine door.

mbm-1469.clue: I’m saving the last yellow square.
mbm-1469.quote: Our community quilt shows the windows of a long apartment block at night. We leave one yellow window unattached until everybody has gathered. The last person in gets to switch on the light.

mbm-1470.clue: I learned the song from a kettle lid.
mbm-1470.quote: At choir rehearsal we couldn’t find the opening pitch. A cook in the hall next door set a lid down with a lovely clear note. We sang from there and saved him a front-row seat.

mbm-1471.clue: I notice the ski tracks that turn purple.
mbm-1471.quote: During our last downhill run the long shadows filled the grooves in the snow. I stopped below the bend to let my brother ski through the violet stripes. He looked like he was skating down a painting.

mbm-1472.clue: I leave a gap for the old gentleman’s cane.
mbm-1472.quote: At folk-dance night we put a chair near the circle so he can set his cane down. He only joins the slow tune, but his feet remember an extra turn the rest of us always want to learn.

mbm-1473.clue: I kept my first broken game cartridge.
mbm-1473.quote: The plastic case cracked, so I drew a little crutch on its paper sleeve. The game still plays. My friends always ask after its recovery before they challenge me to a match.

mbm-1474.clue: I watch the sun go through a colored bottle.
mbm-1474.quote: I put a little amber bottle beside my deck chair and follow its patch of golden light across my book. The letter I was reading to my sister looked as if it had been written in sunshine.

mbm-1475.quote: We left our sandals beside the stones and crossed the cold yard to the outdoor onsen. I drew the little row of shoes in my notebook afterward. They remind me better than any photograph how warm the water felt.
